title: Print Window Weighted Spacing
description: Replace inconsistent window spacing on cover pages with one canonical gap plus weight-normalized row/column/stack sizing. Implement SemioWindowStack and weighted SemioWindowRowTwo/Three macros.
summary:
Fixed three real layout bugs found while visually verifying the recursive window-arrangement rewrite against actual production content (the previous close only checked page-count, not whether rows rendered correctly within that page).

1. **\WindowItem push silently discarded under caller-introduced grouping**: \WindowItem used a *local* \seq_put_right, which TeX undoes when the enclosing group closes. \makecoverpages wraps every conditional row (meta row, institution row) in \bool_if:NT{...}, which — like any extra `{...}` — is exactly the kind of grouping that discarded the push. Replaced the single shared local collector with an explicit, depth-indexed stack of *global* sequences (\semio_window_frame_push:/\semio_window_frame_pop:, keyed by \g_semio_window_depth_int): global mutation survives arbitrary caller-introduced grouping, and per-depth isolation still protects against nested WindowRow/WindowColumn siblings clobbering each other's collection.

2. **TeX dimen-scanner digit/macro-adjacency bug**: `2\semio@chrome@padding` (where padding expands to "0.2em") is read by TeX's dimen scanner as the single dimension "20.2em", not "2 × 0.2em" — the scanner greedily absorbs digits across the macro-expansion boundary. This silently broke both the per-item chrome-overhead formula (titlebar+2×padding+2×hairline+3pt) and, separately, the count×overhead / count×gap total multiplications (same juxtaposition pattern applied to the *already-computed* per-item values). Fixed by never juxtaposing a digit against a macro that expands to a dimension literal — all such multiplications now go through \fp_eval:n on a decimal extracted via \dim_to_decimal:n from a real dim register.

3. **Missing \par after WindowRow's row hbox**: the pre-rewrite code's row renderer ended with `}\par`; my rewrite dropped the \par. Without it, TeX stayed in horizontal mode after each row's `\hbox to \linewidth{...}`, so consecutive rows could collapse onto the same paragraph line instead of stacking as separate vertical blocks — this was the proximate cause of institution/logo rows visually overlapping even though their allocated heights were correct.

All three were isolated via a bisection process using minimal debug fixtures under `.repo/🎫/26/07/10/PRINT-WINDOW-WEIGHTED-SPACING/debug/` (rowbug*.tex, nest3.tex, dimtest*.tex) plus temporary [DEBUG] \typeout instrumentation (removed after diagnosis), since the sandbox's PDF rasterizer is broken — verification is log-based (page-break markers) plus a PDF.js text-position extraction script to confirm rows land at distinct, properly-separated Y coordinates.

Verified: `bun ./script.ts build report forschungsbericht zwischenbericht` (light+dark, 6 PDFs) all exit 0; forschungsbericht and zwischenbericht cover pages confirmed to render all 6 conceptual rows (title, Aktenzeichen/Förderzeitraum/Berichtszeitraum, DOI, institution, logo — zwischenbericht additionally has a 2-cell title row and subtitle) at distinct non-overlapping Y positions on exactly one page.
